passage: In a young solar system, dust grains first stick together through static attraction, building clumps a few centimeters across. Beyond that size, collisions between clumps tend to shatter them, and models in which planets grow one collision at a time stall at this stage. One proposal holds that swirling gas herds clumps into filaments so crowded that their combined gravity overwhelms the gas within a few orbits. There, gravity can ______ them into bodies kilometers wide.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: In the crowded filaments, the clumps' combined gravity takes over all at once, so gravity can "collapse" them into large bodies. "Accumulate" describes the gradual, one-collision-at-a-time growth that the text says stalls. "Bond" describes the sticking that only builds centimeter clumps, and "funnel" describes the gas's herding, which happens before gravity acts.

deletion_test.kept_sentence: There, gravity can ______ them into bodies kilometers wide.
deletion_test.why: alone, gravity could collapse, accumulate, bond, or funnel unnamed material into large bodies; only the earlier sentences show that sticking and one-at-a-time growth fail, that the gas does the herding, and that gravity takes over all at once
